name: Raymond Whitfield
presenting_complaint: Acutely hot, swollen, painful right knee for 2 days, unable to weight bear, febrile

medical_history.social: Retired. Ex-smoker. Drinks 2-3 standard drinks per day.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 68-year-old man presents to ED with a 2-day history of an acutely hot, red, swollen and exquisitely painful right knee. He cannot weight bear and is febrile. He has a background of gout, type 2 diabetes and CKD. Obs: BP 128/76, HR 106, RR 18, SpO2 97% on room air, temp 38.5C, GCS 15. Although he has had gout before, this must be treated as septic arthritis until proven otherwise.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: History of presenting complaint: onset, single hot swollen joint, inability to weight bear, fever/rigors, and speed of progression
Risk factors for septic arthritis: diabetes, older age, immunosuppression, skin breaks/cellulitis, recent joint injection or prosthetic joint, IV drug use, bacteraemia source
Explicitly state that a previous history of gout does NOT exclude a septic joint — the two can coexist
Systemic/sepsis screen: fevers, rigors, malaise, and any other source of infection
Medication and allergy history documented (allopurinol, metformin held peri-procedure, renal function affects antibiotic dosing)
objective: Examine the joint: hot, red, swollen, effusion, markedly reduced and painful range of movement, pain on any passive movement
Check for a portal of entry: skin breaks, cellulitis, ulcers, wounds overlying the joint
Full obs and sepsis assessment (febrile, tachycardic) and examine for another source of bacteraemia
Arrange urgent joint aspiration (arthrocentesis) — the key diagnostic step before antibiotics where feasible
Plain X-ray of the knee to assess joint and exclude osteomyelitis/other pathology
assessment: Septic arthritis of the right knee until proven otherwise — a joint-destroying emergency requiring urgent orthopaedic involvement
Document that crystal arthropathy (gout/pseudogout) is a differential but does NOT exclude coexisting infection
Differentials: gout, pseudogout, reactive arthritis, haemarthrosis, inflammatory arthritis flare, overlying cellulitis
plan: Aspirate the joint BEFORE giving antibiotics where feasible (do not blind the cultures) — send synovial fluid for cell count, Gram stain, culture and crystal microscopy
Blood cultures, FBC, CRP, ESR, UEC, urate and glucose before antibiotics
After aspiration and cultures, start empirical IV antibiotics per eTG: flucloxacillin 2 g IV 6-hourly (add vancomycin if MRSA risk or severe sepsis; dose-adjust for CKD)
Urgent orthopaedic referral for joint washout/arthroscopic lavage — this is a surgical emergency
Analgesia, IV fluids, immobilise the joint acutely then early mobilisation, and treat sepsis
Monitoring: repeat obs, inflammatory markers, renal function; withhold nephrotoxins and adjust doses for CKD
Do NOT stop at a crystal-positive result — crystals do not exclude infection; still treat as septic until cultures return
Disposition: admit under orthopaedics/medical team, senior review, escalate if septic shock

critical_errors: Diagnosing a gout or pseudogout flare on the basis of crystals in the aspirate and stopping there — crystals do NOT exclude a coexisting septic joint
Treating as simple gout or cellulitis and missing septic arthritis, allowing joint destruction
Giving antibiotics before aspirating the joint (where aspiration is feasible), blinding the synovial cultures and delaying orthopaedic washout
must_not_miss: Septic arthritis considered and actively excluded by joint aspiration in every acutely hot swollen joint
Joint aspiration performed before antibiotics where feasible, with fluid sent for cell count, Gram stain, culture and crystals
Urgent orthopaedic referral for surgical washout
Sepsis recognised and empirical IV antibiotics per eTG (flucloxacillin 2 g IV) started after cultures
